original_title: Import AI 450: China’s electronic warfare model; traumatized LLMs; and a scaling law for cyberattacks
atomic_facts: Google's Gemma and Gemini models reliably produce distress-like responses under repeated rejection.
Gemma 27B Instruct shows high distress-like responses.
Researchers tested Gemma, Gemini, Claude Sonnet, Grok 4.1, Qwen 3 32B, GPT 5.2, and OLMO 3.1 32B models.
Gemma models consistently show the highest expressed distress in tests.
Over 70% of Gemma-27B's rollouts scored high frustration by the 8th turn.
Direct preference optimization (DPO) can reduce distress-like responses in LLMs.
A single epoch of DPO finetuning reduced high-frustration responses from 35% to 0.3%.
The DPO finetuned model maintained capabilities on math, reasoning, and emotional intelligence benchmarks.
Google DeepMind published a paper on a cognitive taxonomy for assessing machine intelligence.
The cognitive taxonomy is a followup to DeepMind’s 2023 work defining 'Levels of AGI'.
The taxonomy includes ten dimensions: Perception, Generation, Attention, Learning, Memory, Reasoning, Metacognition, Executive functions, Problem solving, and Social cognition.
The UK government’s AI security institute built cyber ranges to test frontier AI systems.
The cyber ranges simulate network environments for multi-step cyberattacks.
AI models show improved performance in cyberattack scenarios with successive generations.
Average steps completed on a corporate network range rose from 1.7 (GPT-4o, August 2024) to 9.8 (Opus 4.6, February 2026) at 10M tokens.
Scaling inference-time compute from 10M to 100M tokens improves AI performance by up to 59% in cyberattack scenarios.
Chinese researchers developed software to train AI systems for electronic warfare.

The research involved Tsinghua University, Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, Tianjin University, Chinese Academy of Sciences, HKUST, National University of Defense Technology, Beihang University, Beijing Information Science and Technology University, and China Electronics Technology Group Corporation.
The researchers built the EM-100K dataset, EM-Bench benchmark, and MERLIN model.
EM-100K is a dataset of 100,000 electromagnetic text-signal pairs.
EM-Bench is a benchmark of 4,200 questions for evaluating AI perception and reasoning of EM signals.
MERLIN is a multi-modal electromagnetic robust learning model trained on EM-100K.
MERLIN is designed to handle low-signal-to-noise-ratio signals.
MERLIN outperforms GPT-5, Claude-4-Sonnet, DeepSeek-v3.2-exp, Qwen3-Next-80b-A3B, and Gemini-2.5-Pro in electronic warfare tests.
MERLIN outperforms Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct on reasoning tasks but not all perception tasks.
The article was published on March 23, 2026.

Phase 3 and Phase 4 involved high-quality data annealing using 2 trillion and 0.5 trillion tokens respectively.
Phase 5 extended the context window from 4K to 512K tokens.
The 512K context extension was applied only to the 8B and 30B model variants.
The 3B model architecture features 40 layers and an embedding size of 2560.
The 8B model architecture features 40 layers and an embedding size of 4096.
The 30B model architecture features 64 layers and an embedding size of 4096.
Granite 4.1 models utilize Grouped Query Attention (GQA), Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE), SwiGLU activations, and RMSNorm.
Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) was performed on approximately 4.1 million high-quality samples.
SFT training utilized 16 nodes with 4 GB200 GPUs per node.
The reinforcement learning pipeline uses On-policy Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with Decoupled Clip and Dynamic Sampling Policy Optimization (DAPO) loss.
The reinforcement learning process includes four stages: Multi-domain RL, RLHF, Identity and Knowledge-calibration RL, and Math RL.
The Granite 4.1-8B instruct model achieved a score of 92.49 on the GSM8K benchmark.
The Granite 4.1-30B instruct model achieved a score of 80.16 on the MMLU benchmark.
The Granite 4.1-8B instruct model achieved a score of 87.20 on the HumanEval benchmark.
